page: Amazon Web Services i4i.16xlarge is a storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8375C x86_64 processor operating at 3.5 GHz, delivering 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated virtual CPUs. The memory subsystem contains 512 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing an allocation of 8 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources include a bundled 15,000 GB local NVMe SSD array and a baseline network throughput of 38 Gbps, operating without discrete GPUs.

Benchmark testing highlights strength across data processing, compilation, and storage-adjacent computation. The instance recorded a PassMark CPU score of 57600.73, with top-tier results in extended instructions (53507.48), CPU encryption (55427.95), and database operations (26317.04). In application benchmarks, Clang software compilation scored 40738.0, static web serving throughput reached 45.18 GB/sec, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measured 165.49 GB/sec. General multi-core synthetic compute metrics align with median performance profiles, reflecting an architecture focused on balanced execution rather than pure computational throughput.

The combination of 15 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage and a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides significant resource density for disk-bound enterprise systems. Avoiding reliance on network-attached block volumes reduces latency variability and input/output bottlenecks. AWS i4i.16xlarge is suited for I/O-intensive production databases, transactional datastores, distributed NoSQL clusters, search indices, and large-scale web caching infrastructures.
description: Amazon Web Services i4i.16xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual machine utilizing the AWS Nitro platform, powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz with 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 512 GB of DDR4 memory, 38 Gbps baseline network throughput, and 15,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, with no graphics processing units attached. Performance evaluations demonstrate strong results in PassMark database operations, cryptographic processing, and Clang compilation, alongside static web serving throughput of 45.18 GB/sec and 165.49 GB/sec large-block uncached read bandwidth. While synthetic CPU stress results place in the median range, the expansive local NVMe capacity and 8 GB per-vCPU memory allocation offer high efficiency for input/output heavy environments. This system is engineered for transactional relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, search clusters, and high-capacity data ingestion pipelines.
